summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands-on firmware experience across STM32 microcontrollers, building bare-metal C drivers and FreeRTOS-based embedded systems. Comfortable working close to hardware, from register-level GPIO, ADC, and I2C programming to interrupt-driven UART communication and real-time sensor integration. Additional background in Python-based test tooling for hardware data acquisition and in PCB design and fabrication, with a consistent record of debugging embedded systems down to root cause.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture recognition glove for hands free cursor control, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; debugged and resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary, Robotics Club
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and hardware integration end-to-end.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental test visualization in a laboratory environment.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to an STM32 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures across the embedded stack (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) through systematic root-cause debugging; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++; drove five servos with range-gated contact detection using dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over a TCA9548A I2C mux.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
